opts: True: regular and progressive in strength — false: irregular and non-progressive
True: irregular and continuous — false: regular and rhythmic
True: continuous with a fixed intensity — false: rhythmic and progressive
True: regular but decreasing — false: progressive and rhythmic
exp: True labour contractions are regular and increase in frequency, duration and intensity; false labour does neither.

opts: One to two hours after the placenta; physiological chills; observations every 15 minutes
Twenty-four hours after delivery; fever; vital signs taken hourly throughout
Thirty minutes after delivery; rigors; vital signs taken every five minutes
Six hours after delivery; sweating; vital signs taken every half hour
exp: The fourth stage is the first one to two hours after delivery, when the woman may shiver and needs close observation.

opts: Anti-D isoimmunisation, twin-to-twin transfusion, cystic hygroma or placental chorioangioma
An uncomplicated singleton pregnancy with a normal fetus and placenta
Diet-controlled gestational diabetes with a normal liquor volume
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy alone, with raised serum bile acids
exp: Mirror syndrome is the maternal reflection of fetal hydrops, whatever its cause — immune, anastomotic, lymphatic or placental.

opts: Pica, a classic clinical manifestation of severe iron deficiency
Bulimia nervosa, with repeated bingeing and purging behaviour
Hyperemesis gravidarum, with protracted vomiting and ketosis
Chorea gravidarum, with involuntary movements of the limbs
exp: Craving and chewing non-food substances such as clay, raw rice or ice is pica, and it accompanies severe iron deficiency.

opts: Twin A becomes hypotensive and anaemic, exsanguinating into the low-pressure twin
Twin A becomes polycythaemic as blood flows in from the dying co-twin
Twin B becomes hypertensive from the sudden increase in blood volume
No haemodynamic change occurs in either twin at the moment of death
exp: When the monochorionic co-twin dies, the survivor's low-pressure circulation drains the dying twin, which is how the survivor is injured.

opts: Larger than 5 cm, still enlarging, excruciating pain, or associated shock
Any haematoma at all that measures more than 1 cm across
Only once the haematoma has become clinically infected
Only when haematomas are present on both sides of the vulva
exp: Surgical drainage is for a large, expanding or very painful collection, or one that has caused shock; small stable ones are managed conservatively.

opts: A truncated cylinder, with a shallow anterior wall and a deep concave posterior wall
A true cylinder, with anterior and posterior walls of equal depth
Funnel shaped, with a deep anterior wall behind the pubic bone
Cuboid, with a flat posterior wall formed by the sacrum
exp: The cavity is a truncated cylinder: the pubic bone is short in front, while the sacrum forms a long concave curve behind.

opts: A hypertonic contraction from oxytocin; stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, consider terbutaline
An entirely adequate contraction, so the infusion should be continued unchanged
Tachysystole, for which the rate of oxytocin should be increased
A Bandl's ring forming, which requires immediate caesarean section
exp: A contraction lasting 60 seconds or more is hypertonic and usually drug-induced: stop the infusion, turn her and give a tocolytic if needed.

opts: Less postoperative pain, a stronger wound and better cosmesis, but the upper abdomen is not visualised
Faster abdominal entry, although at the cost of more postoperative pain
Better exposure of the pelvis, though the resulting scar is less acceptable
Less bleeding, but a wound that is mechanically weaker afterwards
exp: Transverse incisions heal better and hurt less, but they limit access to the upper abdomen compared with a vertical incision.

opts: Progressive cervical change, or an initial dilatation of 2 cm or more
A fixed dilatation of 5 cm or more with no further change
A fetal fibronectin of 100 ng per mL or more in cervicovaginal fluid
A cervical length of 1 cm or less and no other supporting feature
exp: The current definition drops the add-on tests and requires progressive change, or dilatation of at least 2 cm at presentation.

opts: Uteroplacental insufficiency, giving late decelerations and fetal distress
Accelerated fetal growth from continued nutrient transfer
An increase in amniotic fluid volume from fetal polyuria
The early spontaneous onset of labour well before term
exp: The ageing placenta fails, producing late decelerations on the CTG and fetal distress in labour; liquor falls rather than rises.

opts: The placenta being felt in the vagina, with apparent permanent lengthening of the cord
A sudden gush of blood before the placenta appears at the introitus
The fundus becoming globular and firm on abdominal palpation
The uterus rising higher in the abdomen above the umbilicus
exp: Feeling the placenta in the vagina, with the cord appearing to lengthen permanently, is the surest sign that separation has occurred.

opts: Repeat 400-800 microgram of misoprostol and review her after seven days
Give anti-D immunoglobulin and take no further action at all
Start warfarin to promote expulsion of the retained products
Discharge her immediately, since no follow-up is required
exp: If cardiac activity persists or expulsion is incomplete without bleeding, a further dose of misoprostol is given and she is reviewed in a week.

opts: A previous preterm birth or a short cervix; transvaginal sonography is the tool
All primigravid women, screened by transabdominal sonography
Twin pregnancies alone, screened by magnetic resonance imaging
Preterm prelabour rupture alone, monitored with cardiotocography
exp: Prevention is aimed at women with a previous preterm birth or a short cervix, and transvaginal scan is how the cervix is measured.

opts: Placental insufficiency, with fetal growth restriction and pre-eclampsia
Fetal macrosomia with polyhydramnios in the third trimester
Gestational diabetes mellitus needing early screening
A prolonged pregnancy that runs well past the expected date
exp: A very low PAPP-A reflects poor placentation and is associated with growth restriction, pre-eclampsia and stillbirth.

opts: Donor anaemia and recipient polycythaemia, with normal liquor volume in both sacs
An oligo-polyhydramnios sequence, with equal peak systolic velocities
Donor polycythaemia together with anaemia in the recipient
Abnormal liquor volume in both sacs from the very beginning
exp: TAPS is defined by a large haemoglobin difference without the liquor discordance of classic twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

opts: External aortic compression at the umbilicus, and a military anti-shock garment
The Trendelenburg position with cold packs applied to the abdomen
Vaginal packing with intravenous fluids and nothing further
Fundal pressure combined with an intravenous oxytocin bolus
exp: Aortic compression and a non-pneumatic anti-shock garment buy time while the woman is transferred to theatre.

opts: Ordinary IUGR affects both twins; selective IUGR is monochorionic, one normal and one growth-restricted twin
The two terms mean exactly the same thing and are interchangeable
Selective IUGR is a complication confined to dichorionic twins
Ordinary IUGR affects only one twin of the pair
exp: Selective growth restriction is a monochorionic problem of unequal placental sharing, with one twin normally grown.

opts: Blood, semen, bacterial vaginosis, trichomonas infection and meconium
Contamination with urine, which is the only recognised cause
Contamination with the normal saline used for the examination
The cervical mucus plug alone, which is strongly alkaline
exp: Nitrazine turns blue with any alkaline fluid, so blood, semen, infected discharge and meconium all give false positives.

opts: Decidua, blood, leucocytes and exudate; rubra, then serosa, then alba over 24-36 days
Blood alone; ten days of rubra followed by twenty days of alba
Mucus and pus; alba first, then serosa, then rubra
Amniotic fluid, lasting seven days in total after the delivery
exp: Lochia is decidua, blood, leucocytes and serous exudate, passing through rubra, serosa and alba over roughly 24-36 days.

opts: Give aspirin alone and discharge her for outpatient review
Complete the corticosteroid course while continuing the pregnancy to 34 weeks with monitoring
Deliver the baby before the first dose of corticosteroid is given
Withhold corticosteroids, since they worsen the maternal blood pressure
exp: Without an emergency indication, severe pre-eclampsia before 34 weeks is managed expectantly with a completed course of steroids and close monitoring.

opts: Cervical incompetence, a submucous fibroid and Asherman syndrome
Placenta previa, which implants low and bleeds repeatedly
A previous ectopic pregnancy, which scars the uterine cavity
An ovarian cyst, which distorts the outline of the uterus
exp: Acquired uterine causes of recurrent loss are cervical weakness, cavity-distorting fibroids and intrauterine adhesions.

opts: A vertex with a fully dilated cervix and a rotated head; forceps are preferred in heart disease
A face presentation with the chin anterior; vacuum is preferred in heart disease
A breech presentation, where vacuum is preferred in maternal heart disease
A brow presentation, where forceps are preferred in maternal heart disease
exp: Vacuum suits a rotated vertex at full dilatation; when maternal effort must be minimised, as in heart disease, forceps are preferred.

opts: 0.2 mg intramuscularly, since the intravenous route can cause severe hypertension
0.5 mg intravenously, with the ampoules kept refrigerated
0.2 mg intravenously, from ampoules that have been stored frozen
1 mg by mouth, stored at room temperature
exp: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg is given intramuscularly; the intravenous route risks a dangerous rise in blood pressure.

opts: From 10-12 weeks, with the frog-eye or Mickey Mouse sign from the bulging orbits
From 18 weeks onwards, once the lemon sign has appeared
From 24 weeks onwards, once the banana sign has appeared
From 6 weeks onwards, with the double bleb sign
exp: Anencephaly is recognisable from 10-12 weeks: absent calvarium with prominent orbits gives the frog-eye appearance.

opts: Tachycardia shortens diastolic filling in stenosis, while low resistance helps regurgitant lesions
Progesterone dilates stenotic valves and worsens the pressure gradient
Oestrogen closes regurgitant valves completely during pregnancy
Stenotic lesions are unaffected by the blood volume shifts of pregnancy
exp: Stenotic lesions cannot increase output through a fixed orifice and tachycardia shortens filling; regurgitant lesions benefit from the fall in resistance.

opts: An early fetal echocardiogram performed before 20 weeks
A DIPSI glucose tolerance test in the second trimester
A routine fundal examination at the antenatal visit
Instrumental delivery or manual removal of the placenta
exp: Delivery itself, especially instrumental delivery and manual removal of the placenta, is the commonest cause of a larger feto-maternal haemorrhage.

opts: Renin-angiotensin activation in the donor, causing oliguria, anuria and anhydramnios
Polyhydramnios in the recipient compressing the donor against the uterine wall
Cord entanglement between the two fetuses lying in a single sac
A uterine septum separating the two gestational sacs
exp: The donor twin is volume depleted, activates the renin-angiotensin system and stops making urine, so it becomes the stuck twin in an anhydramniotic sac.

q: When spontaneous delivery of the buttocks does not occur — match the manoeuvre to the breech type: complete breech : frank breech.
opts: Complete breech: groin traction — frank breech: Pinard's manoeuvre in the popliteal fossa
Complete breech: Pinard's manoeuvre — frank breech: groin traction
Complete breech: Lovset's manoeuvre — frank breech: Pinard's manoeuvre
Complete breech: Bracht's manoeuvre — frank breech: groin traction
exp: A complete breech is delivered by traction in the groin; with extended legs the knees must be unlocked first by Pinard's manoeuvre.

opts: Two failed attempts at version, version contraindicated, or transverse lie in active labour
Only when the fetus is known to be alive at the time of diagnosis
Only in a primigravida with an unscarred uterus
Only once the membranes have ruptured spontaneously in labour
exp: A transverse lie at term is delivered by caesarean when version fails or is contraindicated, or once labour is established.
